commit.message:
Record sandbox backends in command execution analytics (#47568)

## Why

Command execution analytics lack the observed sandbox backend. Older execution servers may omit this information, so an unknown backend must remain distinguishable from an explicitly unsandboxed process.

## What changed

- Carry optional `sandbox_type` metadata through command execution items and emit its metric tag as `sandbox_backend` in analytics.
- Propagate the observed backend through unified execution completion and failure events, including asynchronous exits.
- Preserve missing backend information as `None` and mark executed user shell commands as `Some(SandboxType::None)`.
- Exclude the metadata from serialized command items and generated schemas and TypeScript types.

## Testing

Extend tests for missing and explicit executor backends, backend propagation on failed execution, and analytics payloads, including platform-specific backend tags in app-server integration coverage.

GitOrigin-RevId: 178fe46824a6194910802ec02168ed40ee0b2019

Classify rollout read failures by reason and progress (#47565)

## Why

Rollout read metrics record the failure stage and I/O error kind, but these do not distinguish specific zstd failures, task join failures, or a busy reader, nor indicate whether any line was read before failure.

## What changed

Add bounded `reason` and `read_progress` labels to rollout read counters and duration metrics, captured at the first failure. Distinguish OS errors, reader-busy and task-join failures, and known zstd error categories, with `stream_error` as the fallback.

Record whether the failure occurred before or after the first line. Classify blocking-task join failures during both open and read. Keep error messages, file paths, and rollout contents out of metric labels.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6db302900f504bc2860504d81c18017adcef3efc

Add an option to disable multi-agent v2 direct messaging (#47540)

## What changed

Add `features.multi_agent_v2.disable_direct_message`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled, omit `send_message` and `followup_task` while preserving spawning, automatic child results, and the remaining agent management tools.

Require an available message-board `post` tool when this option is enabled for sessions using multi-agent v2 collaboration tools, exempting internal worker sessions.

## Testing

Extend configuration parsing tests and run the message-board subscription/resume scenario with direct messaging both enabled and disabled. Verify post search, subscription behavior, and which collaboration tools are exposed.

GitOrigin-RevId: 72ec22ef0b92fa81e02cdeb058d8b4f93aca3be6

Test interrupted one-shot command launch failure persistence (#47539)

Add a regression test that fails `exec_command` with a missing working directory, pauses command completion, and interrupts the turn before releasing completion.

Verify that the command emits exactly one start and completion, retains its failure status and launch diagnostic, and persists the completion in the rollout. Check that reconstructed history includes the failed command in the interrupted turn.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5962f0791b298ebb05e752138d02b0e0b3af4c63

Route agent lookups and V2 context through `AgentControl` (#47536)

## Why

V2 tools and model context need to use the controller's agent tree even when the session's local runtime has no registry entries.

## What changed

- Add target resolution and direct-child path lookup to `AgentControl`.
- Move lazy root registration into the controller's resolution and listing methods.
- Build V2 subagent context from controller-provided paths, keeping formatting and size limits in the session layer and preserving loaded-first ordering.

## Testing

Extend the V2 spawn and messaging test with an empty session-local registry to cover relative-path resolution, message delivery, and subagent environment context through the controller.

GitOrigin-RevId: c935b34a6d3314e968ba451ff981cf2a223bbfa8

Emit command lifecycle events for unified exec launch failures (#47529)

## Why

When unified exec cannot create a process, command lifecycle events are missing, leaving clients without a command failure notification.

## What changed

Emit start and failure events for terminal process-creation errors in both regular and zsh-fork execution. Report no process ID, an exit code of `-1`, zero duration, and the launch diagnostic, while retaining plugin attribution. Once event publication starts, let it finish even if the caller is cancelled.

Preserve approval rejection handling and retryable sandbox denials.

## Testing

Extend app-server tests to cover pipe and PTY launch failures, plugin attribution on failed launches, and zsh-fork launch failures after approval. Assert failure metadata and check for duplicate lifecycle notifications while retaining approval-decline coverage.

GitOrigin-RevId: 26ed191fc69b903ea4710dd1a6c3b031e8caa4eb

Route session agent operations through `AgentControl` (#47520)

## What changed

- Store `Arc<dyn AgentControl>` in session services and route agent tools, turn admission, usage accounting, completion notifications, and shared settings through the trait.
- Add `AgentControlInit` so delegated and guardian sessions inherit the parent's controller and local runtime.
- Move local registry and context helpers to `LocalAgentRuntime`, keep resume, close, inspection, and status subscriptions on the local controller, and simplify synchronous and infallible trait methods.

GitOrigin-RevId: ad3f213eb483ac524bde56d769f20a78f20989a0

Add explicit background control to image generation (#47484)

## What changed

Add the boolean `transparent_background` argument to `image_gen.imagegen` for generation and editing. Map `true` to `transparent` and `false` or omission to `opaque`, replacing the previous `auto` background setting.

Update tool guidance to request transparency for background removal and cutouts, and to preserve existing transparency during edits unless the user asks to change it.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for transparent, opaque, and omitted background arguments across generation, editing, and code-mode generation. Verify that `null`, string, and numeric values return a validation error without dispatching an image request.

GitOrigin-RevId: b10ac200a619c72cc1787da41b49d65d0cde05dd

Parallelize instruction refresh and tool preparation (#47458)

## What changed

Run `AGENTS.md` and thread-instruction refresh concurrently with capability discovery, MCP setup, and tool construction. Box both preparation futures to keep them off caller stacks while they are live together.

Finish delivering returned instruction warnings even when tool preparation fails or is cancelled. Preserve instruction-error precedence and publish the selected-plugin snapshot only after both branches succeed and cancellation is checked.

## Testing

Add tests covering concurrent preparation, warning delivery on tool failure and cancellation, instruction-error precedence, and plugin snapshot publication. Verify that cancellation does not repeat consumed warnings on the next capture.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6b2d7b091aae2dba67ad154a19bdb0ed0f96f6f7

Extract WebSocket authentication into `codex-websocket-auth` (#47447)

## What changed

Move WebSocket authentication arguments, settings, credential loading, and upgrade authorization into a shared crate using `http` types. Update the app server, transport, and CLI to consume it directly, and remove the `AppServer` prefix from the shared types.

Hide token digests and JWT verification secrets from authentication policy `Debug` output.

## Testing

Move the existing argument validation, capability-token authorization, and signed bearer-token verification tests into the new crate.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1dd20043a3f8efbca55af7eda338b62a62e8fd68

Use secondary text styling for the transcript footer shortcut hint (#47441)

Apply `secondary_text_style()` to the shortcut hint separator and label
so they use a readable foreground color instead of terminal-dependent dimming.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6cd9ced75deca9353c1224d3e5fefc6c4ad6ae8f

Stabilize retry timing and WebSocket tests (#47437)

## Why

Retry timing assertions can fail if the test is descheduled before retry telemetry is emitted, and parallel tests can leave shared tracing callsites disabled for the test subscriber.

## What changed

- Measure retry intervals from the failed request, filter HTTP observations to `/responses`, and track WebSocket stream requests as well as connections.
- Keep a tracing interest-cache guard alive and rebuild callsite interest when installing the telemetry capture.
- Reserve the connection-failure test's port with a bound socket until the recovery server starts listening.
- Wait for the WebSocket warmup request and assert `generate: false` before submitting user input in connection-limit, rate-limit, and overload tests.

GitOrigin-RevId: bba39ea2ac29ac8553ae6184139382f1e6cdc7ac

Allow environment selection updates during an active turn (#47435)

## What changed

- Add `environments` to `TurnSettingsUpdate` to replace the selection for subsequent steps without changing future turns.
- Capture model settings and environments together so combined updates apply or reject atomically, while existing steps retain their captured selection.
- Validate environment IDs, working directories, configuration ownership, and permission requirements against the running turn's selections.
- Preserve executor startup behavior when switching environments and use the step's local working directory for tool hooks.

## Testing

Add coverage for workspace switching and restoration on the next turn, atomic model and environment updates, permission validation, executor connection waits, and replacement of pending environment selections.

GitOrigin-RevId: 02b5c57a78fd594b2aed84fc09d9e99eb97be28c

Apply inherited environment settings at turn boundaries (#47428)

## Why

Thread permission updates could affect later steps of a running turn. Keep inherited environment settings consistent throughout the turn and apply saved updates when the next turn starts.

## What changed

Store active thread defaults alongside selected environments and refresh them when activating a new turn, even when its environment selections are unchanged. Resolve new selections from those active defaults while preserving owner-provided configuration, selection workspace roots, and the local Windows sandbox type.

## Testing

Add a regression test that changes permissions during a paused turn and verifies that both steps retain restricted filesystem access while the next turn receives unrestricted access. Update session and MCP elicitation tests to check that permission changes take effect on the next turn.

GitOrigin-RevId: 37ee44198fa40c138d140974dc90c4177d8c1f4c

Clear pending async question notifications when turns end (#47424)

## Why

An async question notification can outlive its unanswered question and suppress the lower-priority turn completion notification.

## What changed

Clear pending `AsyncQuestion` notifications when collecting question drafts on completion, interruption, or failure, including the error-handling path. Completed turns can then queue their completion notification.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for all three turn outcomes and assertions for error handling and completion after dropped message deltas.

GitOrigin-RevId: 647b2b37acced431fc98fd4f5334c8973a0be241

Preserve history search during background draft recovery (#47423)

## Why

Recovering question answers or interrupted input can cancel an active `Ctrl+R` search or overwrite its preview. Recovery should preserve the search while keeping the recovered input available on cancellation.

## What changed

- Apply background updates to the saved draft without changing the search query or visible preview, including when a query has no match.
- Restore the updated draft on `Esc` or `Ctrl+C`; discard it when accepting a history match. Keep search open when `Enter` has no match to accept.
- Capture the saved draft rather than the preview in draft snapshots, preserving attachments, mention bindings, and pending pastes.
- End search on an explicit fresh draft replacement so cancellation cannot resurrect discarded input.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for recovery on turn completion, failure, and interruption; accepting and canceling search after recovery; Vim undo/redo; pending paste preservation; and clearing drafts after a misalignment policy failure.

GitOrigin-RevId: d3de19bbbcdab2e461c19d47b2b7dca0b28f6ff3

Recover unsent question drafts when TUI turns end (#47422)

## What changed

Clear pending asynchronous questions when a live turn completes, is interrupted, or fails, and append nonblank typed answers to the main composer in question order without submitting them. Preserve existing composer content and input restored after interruption, and retain large answers as paste placeholders.

Cancel history previews and pending Vim commands during recovery while preserving undo grouping and dot-repeat behavior. Skip recovery during replay and keep input cleared after a misalignment policy violation.

## Testing

Add regression tests and snapshots for open and collapsed drafts, buffered typing, answer ordering, repeated completion notifications, large pastes, interrupted queued input, and Vim undo/redo behavior. Update coverage for terminal errors and realtime question expiration.

GitOrigin-RevId: fec109fe8aecb0735a3a5410fbb063b5c5c6e9a1

Use native scrollback for Terminal.app over SSH in auto mode (#47417)

## What changed

- Detect Terminal.app from primary and secondary device attributes during startup on Unix SSH sessions without a detected multiplexer. Ignore signatures inside bracketed paste and leave incomplete replies unknown.
- Use inline mode when Terminal.app is detected and `tui.alternate_screen` is `auto`. Apply the decision before the first startup frame and retain it for later configuration loads. Preserve explicit `always`, `never`, and `--no-alt-screen` overrides.
- Update the `crossterm` dependency revision and lockfiles.

## Testing

Add coverage for terminal signatures, fragmented and pasted replies, probe completion and timeout behavior, screen-mode overrides, and an inline startup snapshot.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9b937824b080f9bd6de29df1d9e84f42a698af46

Support Shift-click to extend transcript selections (#47414)

## What changed

Extend an existing transcript selection with Shift-click while preserving its original anchor and selection unit. Allow continued dragging and repeated extension in either direction, including whole-word selections made by double-clicking. An ordinary click still starts a fresh selection.

## Testing

Add tests for extension in both directions, preservation of selection units, continued dragging, and ordinary-click reset, plus a snapshot of word-selection highlighting.

GitOrigin-RevId: e6208c1bc6260ac26e7cd1f81c752b2c0b375f36

Cache decrypted gateway OAuth secrets per backend (#47413)

## Why

Repeated gateway OAuth credential reads decrypt and deserialize the same unchanged secrets file each time.

## What changed

Add a single-entry cache shared by clones of `LocalSecretsBackend` for `GatewayOAuth`. Reuse decrypted secrets only when the file path, ciphertext hash, and keyring passphrase hash match, and invalidate the cache after writes. Omit cached credentials from the backend's `Debug` output.

GitOrigin-RevId: 91fa03655f5e233d1649f4c2571c5465dfe57f35

Apply shared network policy throughout embedded Codex startup (#47411)

## Why

Application network restrictions need to cover clients created by the TUI and `codex exec` before embedded app-server startup, and remain effective when configuration is rebuilt.

## What changed

- Introduce `EmbeddedNetworkPolicy` to share live policy between caller-owned transports and the embedded app-server.
- Apply loaded requirements before creating telemetry, background HTTP clients, and executor connections. Limit authentication and cloud configuration bootstrap requests to exact endpoints under local policy.
- Preserve the shared policy across TUI session changes, permission-profile rebuilds, and worktree cloud loaders so existing clients observe policy reloads and failures.
- Document application network policy behavior and transport coverage.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for policy activation, reload failure and recovery, retained policy across TUI rebuilds, rejected OAuth and cloud-policy redirects, and workspace network restrictions with `CODEX_API_KEY`. Also cover retaining the caller-selected project during embedded startup.

GitOrigin-RevId: 629009f087b8cb21fc34a1ee7ea6fe95d9e0f2b5

Honor network policy in remote control and recover remote execution (#47410)

## What changed

- Route remote-control enrollment, pairing, client management, and WebSocket connections through the authenticated HTTP client factory. Keep policy denials distinct from authentication failures and wait for policy changes before reconnecting.
- Preserve policy denials through exec-server connection failures so later connection attempts and capability discovery can recover. Keep direct executors running through temporary policy outages while rejecting permanent policy failures.
- Build cached HTTP transports on blocking workers, serialize construction, and retain successful builds after callers time out so request deadlines cover queued construction.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for policy recovery during remote startup, direct registration, accepted WebSocket reconnection, and capability discovery; queued transport construction timeouts; and remote-control WebSocket fallback with invalid custom CA files.

GitOrigin-RevId: c81db18e83de957175bb213d165281ac701089dd

Enforce application network policy for AWS auth and telemetry (#47408)

## Why

AWS credential discovery, analytics, and telemetry used clients that did not share the application's network policy. These requests need to honor destination restrictions and permission revocation.

## What changed

- Route AWS credential and region HTTP requests through the shared HTTP client, and check the signing destination before loading credentials. Skip discovery for static access keys with an explicit region.
- Apply account-scoped policy to Bedrock authentication. Require unrestricted policy for credential exporters and reauthentication commands, and cancel active work when permission is revoked. Document that AWS profile `credential_process` network traffic remains outside the application's HTTP policy.
- Send analytics through the authenticated account's HTTP client factory.
- Guard OTLP log, trace, and metric exports with revocable permits, disable them under destination restrictions, and make managed HTTP exports cancellable. Suppress global Statsig settings while managed policy is active.

## Testing

Add coverage for metadata credential request cancellation, allowed and denied SigV4 destinations, AWS credential precedence and endpoint configuration, and blocked credential exporter recovery. Update telemetry tests for account transitions and managed-policy Statsig suppression.

GitOrigin-RevId: d8a2018bfbbe971ec430699b0d3f86a7a9e1e072

Enforce application network policy across app-server requests (#47407)

## What changed

- Load `application.network` requirements at startup and explicit config/account reloads, applying local policy before authentication and cloud configuration bootstrap.
- Block traffic when policy loading fails, cancel requests that a new policy no longer permits, and reject configuration loads based on superseded policy snapshots. Local requirements edits take effect on the next explicit reload or restart.
- Bind authenticated clients to the current account and revoke them when account ownership changes. Carry policy enforcement through backend requests, realtime connections, workload identity exchanges, and code-mode gRPC streams while preserving gRPC trailers.
- Treat denied credential refreshes as policy errors without retrying them or invalidating stored credentials.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for startup restrictions, reload ordering, cancellation after restrictive or malformed requirements edits, account revocation, gRPC destination denial, workload identity cancellation, and credential preservation after denied OAuth refresh.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0cb4c720a906397e9df06675f01ecf60d741101f

Respect tmux mouse settings in fullscreen and overlays (#47399)

## Why

Codex could enable mouse capture even when the containing tmux session had mouse support turned off.

## What changed

- Probe tmux's `mouse` and `extended-keys-format` settings together, targeting `TMUX_PANE` when available.
- Suppress mouse capture when tmux explicitly reports `0` or `off`, and apply that policy across fullscreen and overlay input changes. Refresh the policy when entering or restoring the alternate screen.
- Preserve normal mouse behavior when the probe fails or the setting is unknown, and retain the keyboard-format fallback for older tmux versions.

## Testing

Add tests for pane targeting, explicit and unknown mouse settings, probe failures, keyboard fallback, and mouse-policy changes across fullscreen and overlays.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7bdd2759207b30a3877e983b489462de7c96e692

Refresh bundled model metadata and instructions (#47397)

## What changed

- Switch the GPT-6, GPT-5.6, GPT-5.5, and auto-review catalog entries to `shell_command` and expand their plan availability.
- Mark `gpt-6-astra` as supporting reasoning-effort updates and disable its experimental-context flag. Add explicit capability and instruction defaults to other entries.
- Update Astra's messaging guidance to recognize authorization from explicitly invoked skills or plugins, with attribution in the final response, and simplify its Default-mode clarification instructions.
- Revise auto-review guidance on autonomy, assumptions, and actions within the user's requested scope.
- Refresh seven scenario snapshots to reflect the updated prompts.

GitOrigin-RevId: b7ed8c413f6451008c982024506009b170e6311e

Retry transient OpenAI file blob upload failures (#47393)

## Why

A single blob upload failure previously aborted the file upload, even for a temporary `503` response or an interrupted stream.

## What changed

- Retry `503` responses and timeout, connection, body, or request errors, with at most five attempts within a shared five-minute deadline.
- Honor `x-ms-retry-after-ms` and `Retry-After`, falling back to backoff when no valid server delay is available.
- Reopen the contents for each retry while reusing the same file record and upload URL. Preserve the initial read permission check and reopen MCP file streams under the same sandbox policy.
- Record retry, recovery, and terminal failure events with a fresh client request ID for each attempt.

## Testing

Add coverage for recovery after `503` responses and interrupted streams, attempt and deadline limits, non-retryable responses, retry delay parsing, and unique request IDs. Extend the restricted-read MCP upload test to verify that both attempts send the complete file contents.

GitOrigin-RevId: 78089ecfd5076313f5784cbbc864df12d082e3b1

Enforce network policy throughout HTTP and WebSocket requests (#47389)

## Why

Destination restrictions and policy revocation must remain effective during redirects, response body reads, and established WebSocket traffic. Policy denials must also survive error handling so callers do not retry them or report a revoked operation as successful.

## What changed

- Route managed HTTP clients through a shared `RequestBuilder` and policy-aware execution, checking each redirect destination before route resolution and retaining a network permit while consuming response bodies.
- Guard WebSocket connection setup, reads, and writes with revocable permits, including independent wakeups for split readers and writers.
- Preserve `TransportError::Policy` through HTTP, SSE, and realtime error handling, and treat policy denials as non-retryable.
- Keep the supplied network policy in plugin startup HTTP requests and propagate response body failures from backend and plugin requests.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for rejection before connecting, revocation during redirect routing and streamed body reads, split WebSocket revocation, realtime writer error propagation, and revoked plugin upload responses.

GitOrigin-RevId: fba36700444c98a8364c09b4dc5452c4d78a90fb

Restore composer hints after clearing selection at the transcript bottom (#47384)

## Why

Selecting text can pause following while the final transcript row remains visible. Clearing that selection could leave an unnecessary `esc latest` hint in place of the composer hints.

## What changed

Only show the return-to-latest footer for paused navigation when the transcript tail is out of view. At the bottom, show selection shortcuts without the earlier-history status, then restore composer hints when the selection is cleared, even if following remains paused. Preserve loading and retry hints.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for selection, clicking away, and scrolling at the bottom with partial and complete history, plus selection above the bottom. Verify retry hints with selected text and update activity expectations and the composer-gap snapshot.

GitOrigin-RevId: aeb2109244d6c3214c945abb51cf469087d03074

Show a voice badge in the agents overview (#47382)

## What changed

Display a `voice` badge on the task whose session owns the running voice conversation, including when a child thread owns it. Refresh the overview after voice controls and realtime conversation resets so the badge clears when background voice closes asynchronously.

## Testing

Add snapshot coverage for a child thread owning voice and a regression test for clearing the badge after an asynchronous background voice close.

GitOrigin-RevId: 815dfad4ce1a31945d2dd0d3f9cecc5abfa419d6

Keep voice conversations running across TUI thread navigation (#47381)

## Why

Switching threads stopped the active voice conversation. Users should be able to view another task while continuing the call on its original thread.

## What changed

- Retain the voice owner's live widget and subscription in the background, routing voice controls, speech, and connection callbacks to that owner.
- Restore the live call and transcript when returning to its thread, without duplicating captions or letting background UI events affect the visible task.
- Preserve undelivered speech and defer background errors until the owning thread is shown.
- Stop background voice on shutdown, disconnect, or removal of the owning session.

## Testing

Extend regression and end-to-end coverage for thread switching during delegated speech, voice control routing, transcript restoration, caption deduplication, and cleanup on disconnect or archive/delete.

GitOrigin-RevId: ce010dce6fa8cd6fa44949a131f3f16e8cb80c4d

Route TUI voice controls through the app (#47380)

## What changed

- Handle voice toggle and mute shortcuts in `App`, and route `/voice`, `/voice stop`, and `/voice mute` through thread-scoped events that ignore requests for a different current thread.
- Allow function-key voice toggle bindings and chords beyond chat, including transcript browsing and search, while preserving existing surface bindings and raw key capture.
- Exit transcript browsing when toggling voice, avoid matching completed chords again, and preserve startup submission handling before dispatch.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for voice chords outside chat, binding conflicts, key capture, transcript browsing, mute dispatch, and startup submission cancellation with draft preservation.

GitOrigin-RevId: c4d110ca8a2e1840247a7fe84cd69c6b7cdb36d7

Add opt-in reasoning status for realtime V3 delegations (#47377)

## What changed

Add `backend_reasoning_status`, disabled by default, to relay public reasoning summaries during active, server-managed realtime V3 delegations.

Use the last non-empty summary from each completed reasoning item, truncate it to 256 bytes at a character boundary, and append it as `[STATUS]` context on the `commentary` channel. Discard queued updates if their delegation is no longer active.

## Testing

Add an integration test covering enabled and disabled behavior, selection of the latest non-empty summary, exclusion of raw reasoning and partial summaries, and delivery without triggering `response.create` or changing the model's reasoning-summary setting.

GitOrigin-RevId: 75ce87dbbbab15a6d9d0ad0b23737738837192fd

Add an opt-in preference for the local MXC sandbox (#47375)

## What changed

Add the default-off `features.prefer_mxc` flag to select MXC for local Windows execution when native support is available and effective network settings do not explicitly forbid local binding. Otherwise, retain the configured backend and legacy setup behavior.

Resolve the preference during config loading and use the effective local backend for execution, network proxy setup, sandbox diagnostics, and `windowsSandbox/readiness`. Preserve the configured backend for remote executors and `config/read`. Explicit `windows.sandbox = "mxc"` remains strict, and command failures do not trigger backend fallback.

## Testing

Add coverage for preference resolution, startup readiness without rewriting configuration, local and remote backend selection across environment updates and child threads, and workspace-write permission context in an agent turn.

GitOrigin-RevId: b51178f0371d38ebb58e41af54a068fca67fa316

Overlap agent metadata reads when resuming a V2 root (#47369)

## Why

Restoring persisted V2 agent identities reads descendant metadata serially, making each storage read wait for the previous one.

## What changed

Read up to eight descendants concurrently while registering identities in graph order, preserving path and nickname reservation order. Skip identities already registered and continue restoring after individual read failures.

## Testing

Add a cold-resume regression test that gates child metadata reads to verify overlap, completes reads out of order to check deterministic path reservation, and injects a read failure. It also verifies that child runtimes remain unloaded until requested.

GitOrigin-RevId: ae90f24875966be83208884937621a6a9eb0d848

Resume model context from the latest compaction boundary (#47365)

## Why

Resuming a compacted thread should use the compaction and its newer records without depending on older turn contexts or restoring stale state from before the compaction.

## What changed

- Stop paginated model-context scans at the newest compaction with `replacement_history` and `window_number`. Fall back to full replay if the newest compaction lacks either field.
- Align reconstruction with that boundary and restore `last_started_turn_id`, previous turn settings, and the multi-agent version from compaction resume metadata. Allow newer completed turns to override the saved settings.
- Keep canonical session metadata alongside the bounded replay and use the same scan boundary for subagent rollout migration.

## Testing

Add coverage for cold resume after mid-turn compaction, bounded/full replay equivalence, missing companion state, settings precedence, and incomplete-compaction fallback.

GitOrigin-RevId: f836464bb5cadd9be4a4e05b5d1679223713fc87

Bound inbound exec-server requests across client transports (#47362)

## What changed

- Enforce an 8 KiB encoded-message limit for requests, unrecognized notifications, and malformed messages received by exec-server clients over stdio, WebSocket, relay, and Noise relay transports.
- Allow process output, exit, close, and HTTP request body notifications up to 2 MiB. Keep responses and errors subject to existing transport limits, and preserve executor-side request limits.
- Read stdio stderr in chunks of at most 8 KiB.
- Drop outgoing server-request `tracestate` values larger than 512 bytes while preserving `traceparent`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for oversized requests across transports, malformed messages, requests wrapped in `RawValue`, fragmented Noise messages, large responses, streamed notifications, and trace-context preservation.

GitOrigin-RevId: 3fb87b6dc334296985ef40983d7276acfe9b9796

Restrict Windows sandbox default object access to the logon session (#47361)

## Why

Shared filesystem capabilities must not grant access to another logon session's processes, threads, or IPC objects. A shared account's implicit owner rights can also allow another logon to rewrite an object's DACL.

## What changed

- Grant full access in the token's default DACL only to the runner's logon SID, removing grants to Everyone and capability SIDs.
- Add an `OWNER RIGHTS` entry granting only `READ_CONTROL` to suppress the owner's implicit `WRITE_DAC` access.
- Close the new token handle if default DACL or privilege setup fails.

## Testing

Add a Windows `AccessCheck` regression test verifying that process memory, thread creation, termination, query, and DACL modification rights remain available to the creating logon but are denied to a simulated other logon sharing the same owner and capability.

GitOrigin-RevId: 94608466ee1b461fe10db1866e80b3988119bdfc

Preserve user prompt URL destinations across terminal widths (#47360)

## Why

User prompt URLs only received explicit hyperlink destinations when they required forced wrapping, leaving other URLs without those annotations.

## What changed

Annotate web URLs before wrapping user messages so their full destinations survive both adaptive wrapping and forced splitting of oversized URLs.

## Testing

Add a regression test and snapshot at widths of 120, 60, and 24 columns, checking URL destinations, line width limits, and matching display and transcript output, including a prompt with an image placeholder and a parenthesized URL.

GitOrigin-RevId: fccae7b76a3613776d7a663c41e699ebad7eebc1

Color paths and URLs in `codex doctor` by check status (#47358)

## What changed

Highlight recognized paths and URLs in check descriptions and details in red for failed checks and cyan otherwise. Extend path recognition on Windows to drive-absolute, UNC, Win32, and NT DOS paths.

## Testing

Add Windows and non-Windows color snapshots covering successful, warning, and failed checks, punctuation, and backtick-quoted paths with spaces. Assert that descriptions and details remain unchanged when color is disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: e8f9982505aa155fd312b12f91a71271effeb35e

Reserve spacing after recaps at the transcript tail (#47355)

## What changed

Reserve a blank row below a trailing recap when the transcript viewport has room. Keep this spacing in layout rather than selectable content, and omit it when a completed or live message follows the recap.

## Testing

Add snapshots covering recap tail spacing across terminal sizes, with and without a next action, and with completed or streaming follow-up messages. Verify that reflowed history retains a single separator between a recap and the following message.

GitOrigin-RevId: f9552931fac4eabd7d72c2b312ffba717257e9e1

Separate thread preparation from execution persistence (#47199)

## Why

Injecting context before the first turn currently forces a full flush. Stores need a preparation checkpoint that can leave disposable context in memory, while local storage must keep prepared context durable before the first user input.

## What changed

- Add `PersistContext::ThreadPreparation` and `CodexThread::checkpoint_preparation()`, and use the checkpoint in `inject_response_items()`.
- Allow stores to defer rollout-derived metadata writes through `record_thread_metadata()`, including during preparation and execution checkpoints. Keep standard metadata updates synchronous.

Add tests showing that preparation and first sampling can proceed without waiting for durable metadata. Cover prepared context in first and follow-up requests, plus durability before first input and restoration after restart, in both legacy and paginated history modes.

Harden gateway OAuth credential persistence and error redaction (#47158)

## Why

Credential I/O can block async workers, and canceled browser logins must not release the credential store lock while a write is still running. Provider errors can also echo secrets from authorization URL query parameters.

## What changed

- Move credential reads and writes to `spawn_blocking`, retaining the cross-process lock until encryption and the atomic write finish, even if the caller is canceled.
- Clear pending rotated credentials during browser login only when stored credentials have changed, preserving recovery after a failed login without overwriting an external login.
- Omit provider response details and request IDs when the authorization URL contains query parameters, matching the existing protection for token and resource URLs.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for authorization URL query-secret redaction and failed browser login after a failed credential save, including retry, expiration, and external-login recovery.

Ignore stale thread-close notifications after resuming a thread (#47155)

## Why

A queued close notification from an old runtime can arrive after the same thread has been resumed. Because thread IDs survive reloads, handling that notification can incorrectly exit the TUI or switch away from the displayed thread.

## What changed

Confirm the displayed thread's status with `thread/read` before handling its close notification. Ignore the notification if the thread is still loaded. Bound verification to five seconds and retry an internal server error once.

If verification fails, reconnect remote sessions. Preserve close handling for embedded sessions, unreadable unpersisted threads, and servers that do not support the request.

## Testing

Add regression tests for stale and genuine close notifications, plus disconnects, timeouts, transient and persistent server errors, embedded-session fallback, and unsupported requests.
